questions.question: If the mode of the following data is 7, then find the value of k.2, 4, 6, 7, 5, 6, 10, 6, 7, 2k + 1, 9, 7, 13
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Mode** is the value that occurs most frequently in a data set.

Count existing frequencies: **6** appears 3 times and **7** appears 3 times.

Since the **mode** is given as 7, the value 7 must occur more times than 6.

This is only possible if the unknown term (2k + 1) is equal to 7.

2k + 1 = 7 → 2k = 6 → k = 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Data set = 2, 4, 6, 7, 5, 6, 10, 6, 7, 2k + 1, 9, 7, 13. Given **Mode** = 7.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a47731ef897c0d6048ed24e8e4be7c0000df995b7d04aa914d264dea84a56ca6.png] 

Frequency distribution of the known terms:

⇒ Number 2: 1 time

⇒ Number 4: 1 time

⇒ Number 5: 1 time

⇒ **Number 6: 3 times**

⇒ **Number 7: 3 times**

⇒ Number 9: 1 time

⇒ Number 10: 1 time

⇒ Number 13: 1 time

For the **mode** to be exactly 7, the frequency of 7 must be the highest in the set.

⇒ Current max frequency is 3 (for both 6 and 7).

⇒ To make 7 the unique mode, its frequency must become 4.

⇒ ∴ 2k + 1 = 7

⇒ 2k = 7 − 1

⇒ 2k = 6

⇒ k = 6 ÷ 2

⇒ k = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Definition of Mode

The **mode** is the value that appears most often in a set of data values. A data set can have one mode (unimodal), two modes (bimodal), or multiple modes (multimodal).

Empirical Relationship

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship between mean, median, and mode is: **Mode = (3 × Median) − (2 × Mean)**.

No Mode Condition

If all values in a data set appear with the **same frequency**, the data set is said to have no mode.</p

questions.question: The arithmetic mean of the observations 39, 49, 59, 60, 70, 80, 90, 93 and 90 is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Assume the **Mean** to be 70 and calculate the **deviations** from it.

Deviations: (39−70), (49−70), (59−70), (60−70), (70−70), (80−70), (90−70), (93−70), (90−70)

Net Deviation = −31 − 21 − 11 − 10 + 0 + 10 + 20 + 23 + 20 = −73 + 73 = 0

Actual **Arithmetic Mean** = Assumed Mean + (Net Deviation ÷ Total Observations) = 70 + (0 ÷ 9) = 70

**∴ The correct answer is 70.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given Observations:** 39, 49, 59, 60, 70, 80, 90, 93, 90

**Total Number of Observations (n):** 9

**Formula Used:** Arithmetic Mean = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/54abd497e7fe85b42a27aa9f9f1e98d3de2ccdbae9037d7de41566c2f893d5fe.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum = 39 + 49 + 59 + 60 + 70 + 80 + 90 + 93 + 90

⇒ Sum = 630

⇒ Arithmetic Mean = 630 ÷ 9

⇒ Arithmetic Mean = 70

**∴ The correct answer is 70.**

**__Additional Information__**

Sum of Deviations

The algebraic sum of the **deviations** of all observations from their **arithmetic mean** is always zero. This property defines the mean as the center of gravity of the data.

Change of Scale and Origin

If each value in a data set is increased/decreased by a constant **'k'**, the **mean** increases/decreases by **'k'**. If multiplied by **'k'**, the new **mean** is also multiplied by **'k'**.

Relationship with Outliers

The **arithmetic mean** is highly sensitive to **outliers** (extreme values), which can pull the mean significantly toward the higher or lower end of the spectrum.</p

questions.question: For a data, if the mean is 28.5 and the median is 32, then the mode using empirical formula is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **Empirical Relationship** between measures of central tendency:

**Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**

Substitute the values: Mode = 3 × 32 − 2 × 28.5

Mode = 96 − 57 = 39

**∴ The correct answer is 39.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Mean** of the data = 28.5

**Median** of the data = 32

**Formula Used:**

For a moderately skewed distribution: **Mode = 3(Median) − 2(Mean)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/edac693489da00dcc38ad76d189ba24efd8440fe6fa02b7c3163d099a5347335.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Mode = 3 × 32 − 2 × 28.5

⇒ Mode = 96 − 57

⇒ Mode = 39

**∴ The correct answer is 39.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relationship

Karl Pearson established this relation for **moderately skewed distributions**: Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean.

Symmetric Distribution

In a perfectly **symmetrical distribution**, the values of Mean, Median, and Mode are all equal (Mean = Median = Mode).

Mean and Median Formulas

Mean = (∑x)/n | Median is the **(n+1)/2th** term for odd n, and the average of **n/2th** and **(n/2 + 1)th** terms for even n.

Skewness

If Mean > Median > Mode, the distribution is **positively skewed**; if Mode > Median > Mean, it is **negatively skewed**.</p

questions.question: Find the median of the data 11, 16, 33, 15, 51, 19, 71, 75, 21, 17.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Arrange the **data** in ascending order: 11, 15, 16, 17, **19**, **21**, 33, 51, 71, 75.

Since the total number of terms (n = 10) is **even**, the median is the **average** of the two middle terms.

Middle terms are the 5th (19) and 6th (21) values.

Median = (19 + 21) ÷ 2 = 20.

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Data:** 11, 16, 33, 15, 51, 19, 71, 75, 21, 17

**Formula Used:**

If n is **even**, Median = [(n/2)th term + (n/2 + 1)th term] ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/02d428aa922d857b7ae4c5b37a2a530645320c7de270926cf69869d5a8401b40.png] 

⇒ Step 1: Arrange data in ascending order: 11, 15, 16, 17, 19, 21, 33, 51, 71, 75

⇒ Step 2: Number of observations (n) = 10

⇒ Step 3: Median = [(10/2)th term + (10/2 + 1)th term] ÷ 2

⇒ Step 4: Median = [5th term + 6th term] ÷ 2

⇒ Step 5: Median = [19 + 21] ÷ 2

⇒ Step 6: Median = 40 ÷ 2 = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Median for Odd Observations

If n is odd, the median is the ((n + 1) ÷ 2)th observation after arranging the data in order.

Empirical Relationship

The relationship between Mean, Median, and Mode is given by: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Mean (Arithmetic Average)

Mean = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations).</p

questions.question: If the mean of a data is 65 and its mode is 23, then the median using empirical formula is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **empirical relation** is: 3 × **Median** = **Mode** + 2 × **Mean**

Given **Mean** = 65 and **Mode** = 23

3 × Median = 23 + 2 × 65 = 23 + 130 = 153

Median = 153 ÷ 3 = 51

**∴ The correct answer is 51.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Mean** = 65

**Mode** = 23

**Formula Used:**

For a moderately skewed frequency distribution, the **empirical formula** is:

**Mode** = 3 × **Median** − 2 × **Mean**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bebd814b32ec8be13a231d6f4de069eea5ede0c7803bb915e6274b8a200dafd0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 23 = 3 × Median − 2 × 65

⇒ 23 = 3 × Median − 130

⇒ 3 × Median = 23 + 130

⇒ 3 × Median = 153

⇒ Median = 153 ÷ 3

⇒ Median = 51

**∴ The correct answer is 51.**

**__Additional Information__**

Symmetric Distribution

In a perfectly symmetrical distribution, the **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode** are identical (Mean = Median = Mode).

Positively Skewed Distribution

If the data is skewed to the right, the values follow the order: **Mean** > **Median** > **Mode**.

Negatively Skewed Distribution

If the data is skewed to the left, the values follow the order: **Mode** > **Median** > **Mean**.

Applicability of Empirical Formula

This formula is an approximation and works best for **moderately skewed** unimodal distributions.</p

questions.question: The arithmetic mean of the observations 3, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 18, 24 and 31 is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Assumed Mean method** by picking a central value like 15.

Calculate **deviations** from 15: −12, −9, −7, −5, −3, −1, +3, +9, +16.

Sum of **deviations** = (−12 − 9 − 7 − 5 − 3 − 1) + (3 + 9 + 16) = −37 + 28 = **−9**.

Correction in **average** = −9 ÷ 9 = **−1**.

Actual **Arithmetic Mean** = 15 + (−1) = 14.

**∴ The correct answer is 14.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The observations are 3, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 18, 24, and 31.

**Formula:** **Arithmetic Mean** = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2f5e41717f56bbcfdda22701f4fb7eec88ea85be35a066851af1d1ebc5c2e083.png] 

⇒ **Total Sum** = 3 + 6 + 8 + 10 + 12 + 14 + 18 + 24 + 31

⇒ **Total Sum** = 126

⇒ **Number of observations (n)** = 9

⇒ **Arithmetic Mean** = 126 ÷ 9

⇒ **Arithmetic Mean** = 14

**∴ The correct answer is 14.**

**__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean Definition

The **arithmetic mean** is the most common measure of **central tendency**, calculated by dividing the sum of values by their count.

Effect of Operations on Mean

If each observation is **multiplied** or **divided** by a constant non-zero value 'k', the resulting mean is also multiplied or divided by 'k'.

Deviation Property

The sum of the **squares of deviations** of a set of observations is **minimum** when taken about the arithmetic mean.</p

questions.question: For certain data, the mode is 24.6 and mean is 20.1. What is the median of that data, using empirical formula?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **Empirical Formula**: 3 × **Median** = **Mode** + 2 × **Mean**

3 × **Median** = 24.6 + 2 × 20.1

3 × **Median** = 24.6 + 40.2 = 64.8

**Median** = 64.8 ÷ 3 = 21.6

**∴ The correct answer is 21.6.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Mode** of the data = 24.6

**Mean** of the data = 20.1

**Formula Used:**

The relationship between **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode** is given by: **Mode = 3(Median) − 2(Mean)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ee20f5b0dd5f8d9edf788498573745c1e52e205b9cd6e83149f7e0b0874e417d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Mode** = 3 × **Median** − 2 × **Mean**

⇒ 24.6 = 3 × **Median** − 2 × 20.1

⇒ 24.6 = 3 × **Median** − 40.2

⇒ 3 × **Median** = 24.6 + 40.2

⇒ 3 × **Median** = 64.8

⇒ **Median** = 64.8 ÷ 3

⇒ **Median** = 21.6

**∴ The correct answer is 21.6.**

**__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relationship

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship is approximately **Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean**.

Symmetric Distribution

In a perfectly **symmetrical distribution** (like a normal curve), the **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode** are all equal (Mean = Median = Mode).

Skewness Types

If **Mean > Median > Mode**, it is **positively skewed**. If **Mode > Median > Mean**, it is **negatively skewed**.

Median from Mean and Mode

The formula can be rearranged to find Median: **Median = (Mode + 2 × Mean) ÷ 3**.</p

questions.question: The median of the observations 4, 14, 11, 8, 7, 8, 9, 12, 4 and 6 is:

The average value calculated by summing all observations and dividing by the total count: Mean = (Σx) ÷ n.

questions.question: If the mean of 22, 25, 27, 24 and x is 26, then the value of x is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume the **mean** is 26.

Find **deviations** from 26: (22−26) = −4, (25−26) = −1, (27−26) = +1, (24−26) = −2.

Net **deviation** of known numbers = −4 − 1 + 1 − 2 = −6.

To balance the **mean** at 26, the deviation of **x** must be +6.

Value of **x** = Mean + Required Deviation = 26 + 6 = 32.

**∴ The correct answer is 32.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Observations = 22, 25, 27, 24, x | Total count (n) = 5 | Mean = 26.

**Formula:** Mean = Sum of observations ÷ Total number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f18518d25fda746f687d3225b2194cb9df6c4faec3b63e548f524b870404d67e.png] 

⇒ Sum of observations = (22 + 25 + 27 + 24 + x)

⇒ Sum = 98 + x

⇒ Mean = Sum ÷ n

⇒ 26 = (98 + x) ÷ 5

⇒ 26 × 5 = 98 + x

⇒ 130 = 98 + x

⇒ x = 130 − 98

⇒ x = 32

**∴ The correct answer is 32.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

The algebraic sum of **deviations** of a set of observations from their **arithmetic mean** is always **zero**.

Effect of Change in Origin

⇒ 17 occurs 1 time

⇒ 18 occurs 3 times

Mode

The value that appears **most frequently** in a data set. A set can have one mode, more than one mode (multimodal), or no mode at all.

Empirical Relationship

Median

**Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**
